commits: e67fef9 fix: read an object header with comments between its tokens near a row and in a rebuild (Refs #261). PdfFileReader.TryReadHeaderBackwards walks back over white space. Where the white space it crosses holds CR or LF and the line that end of line closes holds a %, it lexes that line from its start with PdfLexer and takes the line's last tokens (digits alone), and it passes a line that holds only a comment. Otherwise it reads digit runs as before. The walk is linear and allocates nothing (private struct HeaderNumbers). Two redundant guards are removed. ChainFiles.HiddenHeader(n) now writes 'n +0 obj'. HandWrittenFile.CrossReferenceStream and NearbyFiles get optional header parameters. threat-model.md and concepts/diagnostics.md are updated.

b09f981 fix: stop a damaged stream at an object header with comments between its tokens (Refs #261). HeaderText carries three parts into each read: the runs of white space and digits (as before), a lead (what a walk across the end of line before the line the read starts in takes, at most two numbers plus a token-start byte), and the state of that line lexed so far. The line state lives in a new internal struct LineTokens, a resumable per-line lexer that matches PdfLexer, holds a few fields whatever the line's length, and passes white space, strings, names and digit runs with one SearchValues search each. PdfObjectParser.IsHeader, MayBeHeaderBytes and HeaderUndecided now only check that the tokens are digits alone; the lexer already reads past comments between tokens. Updated texts: the HeaderText.FindHeader remarks (old HeaderText.cs:131-133), concepts/diagnostics.md:52-55, reference/diagnostics.md syntax.truncated-object (now line 122, not 116), reference/validation-rules.md (with a [#261] link definition), and threat-model.md (rows for the parser's header rule and the stream-end search, plus what bounds a comment line).

TD6 removes the early return at Beyond; Math.Min keeps the value at Beyond, so only speed changes.
deviations: The stream-end rule follows the scan through a resumable line lexer, so a comment line has no length bound of its own (ADR 34: no new bound). What bounds it is the search's own reads. The line state carried between reads is a few fields whatever the line's length, and nothing is read past what the search reads now. Within one read a line is lexed at most twice (by the walk of one obj and by the walk that carries the read's end), and the line the read starts in is lexed once as it is read. This is stated in the FindHeader remarks and in the threat model.
LineTokens is a lexer separate from PdfLexer, because it must resume across reads. A property test holds it to PdfLexer's last two tokens over randomly cut lines.

Behavior change beyond the flipped rows: digits that a comment ends with (e.g. '% a note 7\n0 obj') are no longer an object number for the stream-end rule. The old rule took them; the new one matches the scan.

The stream-end search costs more on pathological lines (about 4x on comment-headers-not, about 2.3x on comment-lines, about 1.6x on a single 4 MB line or an unclosed string). It stays linear and allocates nothing more. Realistic text, binary data and the StreamLengthBenchmarks are unchanged.

Redundant guards were removed where the new walk makes them unreachable: the index<0 and whitespace-before-generation checks in TryReadHeaderBackwards, and a guard in HeaderText.TryFindStart (its comment says why).

Line references in the brief had moved: the HeaderText text was in the FindHeader remarks, and the reference/diagnostics.md row is now line 122, not 116. reference/validation-rules.md also stated the old rule and was updated.

The prototype refused only /Index and /Size references and resolved /Index elements through NumberingFault. Reason: one rule for values ISO 32000-1 makes direct (7.5.8.2), and no older row standing on what an object a section placed holds, for a section whose rows are lost. Data structure. The prototype allocated two Lists per refusal and sorted every kept range again (O((R+n) log(R+n))). Here the ranges sit in a (long First, long End)[] rented from ArrayPool with a count. Each stream's ranges are sorted alone, then merged in one pass with the kept ones into a second rented array, at a cost of O(n log n + R) with R at most 4,096. Arrays go back to the pool, and the last is released in Initialize's finally with the other chain-only state. Measured: the bounded prototype allocated 14x for 4x the streams; this allocates 4.02x.

Loop structure. The hand-on runs inside the not-Read branch, after the sections == 1 return and before the relocation branch, and goes straight to its /Prev with continue. The lost stream's position is not added to the read-positions set, since it was not read: a /Prev naming the stream again reports '…which the chain has already named', not '…already read'. RefuseDeclared runs before ReportLostSection so the message can say which numbers are refused. The diagnostics come out in the decided order (section-unreadable before the /Prev's own report), because the refusal reports nothing.

Message. For a stream that hands its /Prev on, the xref.section-unreadable tail replaces the old one. It reads 'The chain goes on through its /Prev; the objects it numbers that no section read before it indexes are looked for by rebuilding the index, rather than taken from an older section's rows.', or '…every object no section read before it indexes…' where every number is refused. Other sections keep the old tail.

deviations: Mirroring #156: the code does not add a separate JudgeStreamPastGuard as the prototype did. When a guard stopped a section's rows, its /Prev and /XRefStm are fed into the whole read's own /XRefStm branches and the loop head. The pastGuard flag lets those branches run, except that nothing in the file not yet reached is read. The naming-again record, ReportNoStream, the NotFound record for an /XRefStm outside the file (with NamingTrailer and its position recorded), the /XRefStm that names what its /Prev names, and the ReachedBefore positions are therefore the whole read's by construction. That is what the critic's decision and stage 8's open point asked for.

An /XRefStm that names what the table's /Prev names, in the file, past a guard: this case is reported as hybrid-stream-lost (Warning) and hybrid-stream-wrong (Error), and the /Prev stays the guard's. The decisions only said that an /XRefStm the chain read that names no stream is reported. Reason: the two offsets being equal is visible without reading past the guard, and a guarded read reports what it saw (stage 8's principle). The `what` text differs, 'the section its /Prev names too, past the guard that stopped the table', because the whole read's 'which the chain reads through that /Prev' would be false there. Outside the file, the whole read's text is kept, since the /Prev is judged there too.

Stream filling the index: when the index fills at a stream, its /Prev now goes into _previousPastGuard like the rows-cut case (`if (rowsCut || _indexFullAt >= 0)`). As a result the loop's old `if (_indexFullAt >= 0) break;` is removed. A full index now always leaves previous and hybrid at -1, so the loop needs no special case for it.

Simplifications of the prototype: its `endedByGuard &&` clause is dropped, being implied by the fields being set. So is `section.TrailerCutByLimit ? -1 : previous >= 0 ? previous : _previousPastGuard`, replaced by previous and hybrid taken from the two fields.

JudgeLinksPastGuard is called at the end of ReadTrailerPastRows, which both rows-cut call sites reach, rather than after each call. It no longer sets ChainHiddenByGuard or ChainHiddenAtStream as the prototype did. That assignment was dead: with rowsHidden, LeadsPastIndex catches a reference that meets an object a guard cut before Follow can report it, so hidden is always null. A test asserting the 'names older sections, but its /Prev ... cut' finding failed under every guard, which showed it. That test now asserts that the link stays the guard's.

One notion of 'already reached' (Q9, stage 5's open point): ReachedBefore is used at the pastGuard loop top, in NamesSection (and so NamesOlderSection), and in the TrailersHiddenByGuard line at the hybrid break. All three used visited.Contains before. Tests with a section found moved kill the reversion (N3, H11).

deviations: Message wording. The decision fixes 'defines' and CountText, not the sentence. The reader says: 'The cross-reference stream {naming} names at offset {o} gives {N row(s), grouped} a reserved type: {first}[, the first of them]. ISO 32000-1 defines types 0, 1 and 2, and reads any other as a reference to the null object (7.5.8.3): the row was read so, and no older section's row stands for its object.' The plural form says 'the rows were read so … their objects'. The rule says: '… gives {N} a reserved type: {first}[, the first of them]. ISO 32000-1 defines types 0, 1 and 2, and reads any other as a reference to the null object (7.5.8.3), as the reader does.' The rule's remedy: 'Rewrite the cross-reference stream with a row of type 0, 1 or 2 for each object it numbers: type 0 for one that is free.' The prototype's 'allows … only' is gone, and both counts use CountText.Grouped.

Hook. The reader report is called right after ReportSectionReadInPart at both of its call sites: the section kept, and the /XRefStm stream read. It is not called after ReportLostSection or in the hand-on branch, as the prototype did. A stream's rows are read last in its reading, and nothing after them makes it Malformed, so a lost section never holds rows that were read. A call there could not be reached by any input and would leave an unkillable mutant. A first section that leads to a rebuild reports nothing, as decided.
